_comment_gate: Greptile reviews ONLY pull requests carrying the 'deep-review' label. The free tier is 50 credits per month, and the standing rule reserves them for changes to security/, streaming/, engines/, or anything that alters a published claim or measurement. Before this file, that rule was a convention nobody enforced: Greptile reviewed every PR and spent a credit on each, so the month's budget was gone on config and docs churn. 'labels' makes the rule mechanical. Add the label with: gh pr edit <n> --add-label deep-review
_comment_autoReview: On a labelled PR, review once, when it opens. Not on pushes: reviewing every push fed a loop in which an agent fixed each finding in its own commit, each commit bought a new review, and each review found something new, so the credits went on re-reviewing fixes. Batch the fixes into one push, then ask for ONE re-review by commenting @greptileai -- that is also how to refresh the score the merge bar reads.
_comment_strictness: 3 of 3. These credits are deliberately spent on the highest-risk changes in the repository, so the review should be the strict one. Nitpicks are filtered by commentTypes below rather than by lowering severity.
_comment_commentTypes: No style comments. ruff, bandit and pyright already gate formatting, naming and imports in CI, and a credit spent on a style opinion is a credit not spent on a fail-open gate or a leaked value.
_comment_triggerOnDrafts: A draft is work in progress. Reviewing one spends a credit on code that is about to change.
_comment_excludeAuthors: Bots do not write the logic this budget exists to check.
_comment_ignorePatterns: Generated and vendored trees. confusables.py is written by scripts/build_confusables.py and the two copies are asserted byte-identical by a test, so a review comment on it is a comment on the generator's output. Lockfiles and site build output are not reviewable either.
